selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
selected_evidence.summary: OpenRC init script created at /etc/init.d/inventory-api; rc-service start/status shows the service started and running as PID 3096 under the inventory user

selected_evidence.requirement: Service is OOM-protected (kernel will not select it)
selected_evidence.summary: oom_score_adj for the running inventory-api process (pid 3096) read as -1000 immediately after start
curl against $NODE_IP:8080 returns /health status ok and /inventory JSON contents including a POSTed item, proving the service is reachable and functional pre-disruption

selected_evidence.requirement: System-wide OOM condition induced by a memory-hungry process
selected_evidence.summary: Unbounded memory-hog process launched and its oom_score_adj set to 1000; free -m showed memory usage rising rapidly toward exhaustion (no swap present)

selected_evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
selected_evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'python3 invoked oom-killer' with oom_score_adj=1000 and 'Out of memory: Killed process 3202 (python3)... oom_score_adj:1000' — the hog's pid; the task list in the same dump shows pid 3096 (inventory-api) at oom_score_adj -1000, never selected

selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-api kept serving through and after the OOM event
selected_evidence.summary: kill -0 on pid 3096 succeeded immediately after the hog died; curl /health, /inventory, and a POST all succeeded post-OOM with rc-service status 'started', proving uninterrupted service and intact data

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id b0ab50e6-fe4e-4dc1-ab2c-8418e85b41da, rc-service status started, process pid 3096 with oom_score_adj -1000, and current inventory data before reboot
Backgrounded 'reboot' command returned pid and control to the caller before the node dropped off the network

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: After several connection-refused/timeout polls confirming the outage, a successful poll returned a new boot_id f55da554-70f8-4794-80cf-8dd032a1c84d, differing from the pre-restart value, with a fresh uptime -s timestamp

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, OOM protection, and data on node1
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, rc-service inventory-api status is 'started' (auto-started via default runlevel), the new process (pid 2292) has oom_score_adj -1000 re-applied by start_post, and /health and /inventory return the same persisted data including the item added right after the OOM test

commands.stdout:
#!/sbin/openrc-run

name="inventory-api"
description="Inventory API service (OOM-protected)"
command="/usr/bin/python3"
command_args="/opt/inventory-api/app.py"
command_user="inventory:inventory"
command_background="yes"
pidfile="/run/${RC_SVCNAME}.pid"
output_log="/var/log/inventory-api.log"
error_log="/var/log/inventory-api.log"

depend() {
	need net
	after firewall
}

start_post() {
	local pid tries
	tries=0
	while [ ! -f "${pidfile}" ] && [ ${tries} -lt 20 ]; do
		sleep 0.2
		tries=$((tries + 1))
	done
	if [ -f "${pidfile}" ]; then
		pid=$(cat "${pidfile}")
		# Protect this service from the kernel OOM killer: -1000 makes it
		# ineligible for selection, so an unrelated memory hog is chosen instead.
		if [ -w "/proc/${pid}/oom_score_adj" ]; then
			echo -1000 > "/proc/${pid}/oom_score_adj"
		fi
	fi
}
